payload.rationale: The supplied Freddie Mac observations rise from 6.65% on August 20 to 6.95% on September 17, including a 19-basis-point increase in the latest week. At the usual two-decimal publication precision, YES requires September 24's first published PMMS rate to be at least 7.02%, a further increase of 7 basis points. Recent upward movement makes that plausible, but five observations do not establish that the unusually large latest increase will persist. My judgment allows modest upward momentum while substantially discounting mechanical extrapolation, leaving the probability close to, but below, one-half. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the latest jump may have reflected a temporary repricing that stabilizes or reverses. The strongest reason it could be too low is that sustained upward pressure, or delayed transmission into mortgage offers, could produce another increase comfortably above the required 7 basis points. Those mechanisms are assumptions, not observed facts in the supplied evidence.
limitations: Only five prior weekly observations are supplied; they do not support a fitted transition distribution.
No contemporaneous Treasury yields, lender quotes, or observations for the September 24 measurement period are available.

The probability is a judgmental estimate, not a calibrated statistical-model output. Resolution depends on the first published September 24 Freddie Mac PMMS value, not later revisions or another mortgage-rate series.
